name: Technical shell alpinism
region: United States, the Alps and the Himalaya
summary: The alpine kit built around a waterproof, breathable membrane shell with taped seams, over a fleece mid layer. A synthetic base, made for speed and low weight.

philosophy.core_thesis: A shell must stop rain and let sweat out. A membrane with pores that block water and pass vapour, seams that are sealed, and a cut that moves with the climber.
design_principles: Laminate a membrane with pores of about 0.2 micron between two nylon layers.
Tape every seam with a heat-sealed strip, so that water cannot pass the needle holes.
Weigh a full hard shell at 400 to 600 g, and a light shell at 250 g or less.
Cut the hood to fit over a helmet and move with the head.
Add a water-resistant zip with a storm flap on the front and a vent zip under the arm.
Cut the arm with an articulated elbow and a long back, so that the hem stays down when the arm is up.
Wear a base layer, a fleece and the shell, and no cotton.
anti_patterns: Cotton next to the skin that holds sweat
A heavy, stiff shell that blocks the arm
A hood too small for a helmet
A shell with no vent for body heat

silhouette.shape: A close, articulated hooded shell with a long back, sealed zips and a snug cuff, worn over a fleece.
silhouette.line: A sculpted shoulder and arm that follow a reach, and a longer back hem that drops below the seat.
silhouette.fit: Trim, with room for a mid layer and a harness; the articulation lets the arm rise without a lift of the hem.
silhouette.proportion: Jacket to the hip, longer at the back; roughly 1 to 1.2 chest to hip over the layers.
rules: Make the hood adjustable at three points, to fit a helmet.
Tape each seam and seal each zip against rain.
Add a pit zip for vents and a chest pocket above the harness line.
Cut the hem long at the back, with a drawcord at each side.
Fit a stiff peak to the hood for rain and snow.

fabrics.rule: Choose a laminated membrane shell of nylon, a fleece for the mid layer and ripstop for the light parts, and use no cotton. The whole kit must dry fast.

methods: three-layer laminate of face, membrane and liner
adjustable helmet hood with a peak
sealed zips with a storm flap
construction.closures: A water-resistant coil zip with a storm flap, a hook-and-loop cuff and a drawcord at the hem and the hood.
construction.details: A helmet hood with a peak, a chest pocket above the harness, pit zips, a long back hem and a taped seam at each join.

surface.pattern: Colour blocks on the shoulder and the hood; no print.
surface.gloss: The face fabric at 10–30 GU; fleece at 1–3 GU.
surface.wear: The water-repellent finish fades at the shoulder and the cuff; the wearer washes and heats the shell to bring it back.

palette.strategy: Bright primary shells for rescue and for photographs, over dark fleece and base layers.

processes: lamination of the membrane to the face cloth
making.scale: Made in factories to a tested spec; each shell goes through a rain test and a seam check.
making.signs: A taped seam, a helmet hood with a peak, a pit zip, a long back hem and a sealed coil zip.

pieces.form: Three-layer hardshell with a helmet hood and taped seams
Mid-layer fleece jacket with a high collar
Light pullover shell for the approach
Belay jacket with a hood and a ripstop shell

evidence.title: Water drops on a shell jacket with taped seam

emotion.target_response: A sense of speed, precision and control over the weather: the wearer looks ready for hard use.

use_cases: a product brief for a hardshell jacket
an image prompt for an alpine scene
a costume brief for a 1980s climbing film
a study note on membrane cloth
avoid_when: the brief is a heritage, waxed jacket
the brief is warm, soft wool dress

modifiers.how: Dye the shell black, add more pockets and straps, and cut a wider, clean line.
Swap the helmet hood for a plain one, add a fleece and bright colour blocks.

sources.title: Wikipedia: W. L. Gore and Associates

ornament_level.note: Colour blocks on the shoulder and the hood; the shell carries no other ornament.
